'''Mou Chung-yuan''' ({{lang-zh|t=牟中原|p=Móu Zhōngyuán}}; born 1949) is a Taiwanese chemist. He was the Deputy Minister of the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Taiwan)|National Science Council]] (NSC) of the [[Executive Yuan]] in May 2012 until March 2014.<ref name="nsc">{{cite web|url=http://web1.nsc.gov.tw/ct.aspx?xItem=15026&ctNode=940&mp=7|title=科技部 Ministry of Science and Technology|publisher=web1.nsc.gov.tw|accessdate=2014-08-23}}</ref>

== Career ==
Mou earned a bachelor's degree from [[National Taiwan University]] in 1970 and pursued graduate study in the United States, completing his [[Ph.D.]] in chemistry at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1975 under professor Ronald Lovett.<ref name="asbio"/> Before assuming his role at the National Science Council, Mou was a professor of chemistry at [[National Taiwan University]]. He was elected a member of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 2013,<ref>{{cite news |title=4 Taiwan academics elected to TWAS |url=https://taiwantoday.tw/news.php?unit=10&post=20342 |access-date=16 March 2022 |work=Taiwan Today |date=4 October 2013}}</ref> and the [[Academia Sinica]] in 2016.<ref name="asbio">{{cite news |title=Chung-Yuan Mou |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=696&_lang=en |access-date=16 March 2022 |agency=Academia Sinica}}</ref>
